justification: Standard: adds a production table and a trigger on dcp_chapter_registry (migration 126) plus a backfill script. Not Minor: it touches the live pipeline's registry table and creates evidence data. Not Critical: new objects only, no existing row or column changes, the trigger cannot block a write, and the ledger is append-only.

pre_impl.existing_data: R2 already holds 803 council PDFs (2.2 GB) from 2026-02-28 under source-pdfs/dcps/{council}/{version}/{chapter}.pdf; r2_monitor writes each new version to a new path and never deletes. dcp_chapter_registry keeps only the current path and (since migration 125) staged_* columns. dcp_monitor_chapter_results holds daily outcomes since 2026-10-22.
pre_impl.assumption_mismatch: I first told the owner no dated archive of old PDFs existed. That was untested; the bucket listing shows the files exist and only the ledger of when each was held is missing.
pre_impl.new_vs_existing: New table plus trigger plus backfill. Nothing in r2_monitor or any extraction script changes: a trigger on the registry captures every writer (monitor, confirm_chapter, repoint, populate scripts, staged commit).
pre_impl.external_source_error: captured_at is the R2 LastModified (when our copy was stored), not the council's publication date; R2 ETag is MD5 for single-part uploads, not sha256. Both limits are stated in the migration header and plan.
pre_impl.user_failure_mode: If the ledger were wrong, an evidence statement could name the wrong file for a date. Mitigation: append-only, unique per (file, event), limits stated, and 'nothing recorded' is returned as no row, never a guess.

falsifiable_check.fails_when: The registry trigger loses its exception handler, or the ledger loses its append-only guard, or the backfill guesses a path shape it cannot read.
falsifiable_check.observed_red: Mutation 1 (exception handler replaced by RAISE EXCEPTION) made test_the_registry_trigger_can_never_block_a_write FAIL (1 failed, 16 passed). Mutation 2 (append-only guard replaced by AFTER INSERT) made test_the_ledger_is_append_only_and_idempotent FAIL (1 failed, 16 passed). Restored: 17 passed.

functions.name: parse_key
functions.output: council, version label and chapter key, only for the exact five part PDF shape
functions.if_none: returns None so the caller reports the key as skipped and never guesses

functions.name: rows_from_objects
functions.input: a list of R2 listing entries with Key, Size, ETag and LastModified
functions.output: insert tuples for the ledger plus a list of skipped keys
functions.if_none: an entry without a date or a readable key goes to the skipped list, not into the ledger

values: N/A - no value is derived from a database or API reading; the script only copies object names, sizes, ETags and dates from the R2 listing.

queries.purpose: Insert one ledger row per R2 file, once
queries.where_clause: INSERT ... ON CONFLICT (r2_key, event) DO NOTHING (no WHERE; idempotent by the unique key)

queries.purpose: Count ledger rows before and after to report how many were added
queries.where_clause: SELECT count(*) FROM dcp_source_versions (no filter needed: new table)

break_it.scenario: The registry trigger raises an error while the monitor is updating a chapter.
break_it.what_happens: A council intake or the daily monitor would fail because of the logging step.
break_it.how: The trigger body catches every error and turns it into a warning; a test pins this and a mutation proved it.

break_it.scenario: Someone edits or deletes ledger rows to change the history.
break_it.what_happens: The evidence of which file was held when would be unreliable.
break_it.how: BEFORE UPDATE OR DELETE and BEFORE TRUNCATE guards raise an error; row level security hides the table from the public key.

break_it.scenario: The backfill is run twice or run after the trigger has already logged some files.
break_it.what_happens: Duplicate rows would double count versions.
break_it.how: UNIQUE (r2_key, event) with ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING; the script prints rows before and after.
break_it.repro: Run the script with --apply twice and compare the added count (second run adds 0).

break_it.scenario: An R2 key has an unexpected shape, such as an extra folder level.
break_it.what_happens: A wrong chapter name could be recorded and later cited as evidence.
break_it.how: parse_key accepts only the exact five part shape; everything else is printed as skipped.

post_merge.manual_verify: Yes - migration 126 must be applied to production BEFORE merge (schema contract CI reads the live catalog); then run the backfill dry run, apply, and check ledger rows equals the R2 object count (803 at 2026-11-18).
